title: Permit
description: A permission granted by government to do something otherwise restricted: build, demolish, trade, occupy, hold an event, serve alcohol. Building permits and business licences are the highest-volume records most governments hold. schema:GovernmentPermit is a real type and supplies the grant itself - issuedBy, validFrom, validUntil, validFor, validIn - but nothing about the application that produced it, which is where most of the public interest lies. Those fields are minted here.

permitNumber.description: The reference the authority uses publicly.

name.description: The permit's title, e.g. 'Building permit, 123 Main St'.

description.description: What is permitted. For building work, the description of works as submitted.

url.description: Where this permit's canonical human-readable page lives.

identifier.description: Any scheme-qualified identifiers for this permit beyond its `@id`.

permitType.description: termCode from the PermitType code list. Deliberately generic: the same permission is a building permit, planning permission, a permis de construire or a Baugenehmigung depending on the country.

permitStatus.description: Where the application has reached. Required: a permit record without a status cannot be told apart from an application that was never decided.

workType.description: For construction permits, the nature of the works.

issuedBy.description: The GovernmentOrganization granting it. Real schema.org property.

validIn.description: The Jurisdiction the permit is valid in. Real schema.org property.

applicationDate.description: When the application was received. With decisionDate this is what makes processing time measurable, which is the question residents and developers actually ask.

decisionDate.description: When it was granted or refused.

validUntil.description: When the permit expires. Absent means no fixed expiry.

completionDate.description: For works, when they were signed off.

premises.description: Where the permit applies: an address, a parcel identifier, or a reference to a `Place` - whichever the authority holds. A residential building permit ties a named applicant to a home address, so see the privacy section of the profile README before publishing applicant details alongside this.

applicant.description: Who applied, as a reference to an Organization. Optional by design: where the applicant is a private individual rather than a business, publishing their name against their home address is a disclosure decision the authority must make deliberately, not a field the schema demands.

declaredValue.description: Declared value of the works, where the authority collects it.

condition.description: Conditions attached to the grant. A permit granted subject to conditions is not the same as one granted outright, and only this field shows the difference.

relatedLegislation.description: The provision the permit is granted under - a zoning chapter, a licensing act. Joins to the code profile.

sourceDataset.description: The `Dataset` this record was published as part of.
